decay.note: Authored from botanical descriptions of Oregon white oak: leathery blades 5 to 15 cm, deeply cut into rounded lobes, paler beneath, on petioles of 1 to 2 cm, yellow-brown in autumn, drying brown and crinkled and slow to rot; acorns 2 to 3 cm. The crown wears sprigs of toothed leaves; a fallen leaf seen whole takes the lobed shape. Colours and curl chosen by eye; numbers plausible, not measured.

look.note: Authored: the drawn look's mean hue at the brightness chosen by eye for this species' litter, the relief the drawing has, and a tile its pieces repeat on unseen. PlantGen's litter tests check the hue and relief against the drawing.
